citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility did not perform daily observation so that timely and accurate information on the problems of animal health
were conveyed to the veterinarian. On June 4, 2026 a juvenile cavy was euthanized by the attending veterinarian (AV)
due to it succumbing to infected wounds. An animal caretaker noted the young cavy had raw, irritated, and reddened skin
on June 4, 2026 but the facility did not note its progression prior. A video was recorded of this animal and sent to the
attending veterinarian on June 4, 2026, showing the extent and severity of the animals wound. This area was infested
with crawling larvae and a fly was seen on it. The wound was brown in color and appeared to extend into subcutaneous
tissue. At the recommendation of their AV the animal was euthanized. The AV was contacted and she informed the
inspector that the young cavy was euthanized the day it was presented to her since it was very lethargic and wasn’t doing
well. She noted the animal had maggots along her back and abdomen. AV indicated facility failed to observe that this
animal was sick and had apparently been so for several days prior to the June 4th observation.
The presence of blow fly larvae indicates this wound was present prior to when the issue was first observed and relayed
to the AV. Failure to observe each animal daily may result in not observing health changes leading to severe harm or
injury to animals that cause more than momentary pain.
Each exhibitor shall conduct daily observations of all animals to assess their health and well-being. A mechanism of direct
and frequent communication is required so timely and accurate information on problems of animal health, behavior, and
well-being is conveyed to the attending veterinarian.
Correct from this date forward, June 30, 2026.

The facility is not ensuring that animals housed together are compatible.
• Rosemary, an adult female Patagonian Cavy, was noted on the April 16, 2026 to have had a healing wound on the top
aspect of her right lower leg. On 6/29/26 facility representative was asked how these wounds were acquired. She stated
staffing changes were made and was not aware what elicited the wounds.
• Lavender, an adult female Patagonian Cavy, was taken to their attending veterinarian on June 3, 2026 due to several
lacerations and a gait abnormality. The exam noted puncture wounds on the top of her head near the left eye. Also noted
were superficial abrasions on the rear hocks along with a superficial laceration on her left shoulder. For history, the exam
record states she had been bullied by the other cavies in the enclosure.
• On June 4, 2026 a juvenile Patagonian cavy, offspring of Rosemary, was observed with blow fly larvae on red and
irritated skin lesions. Phone correspondence by the keeper showed that their attending veterinarian suspected these
larvae were a result of several small bites on the rump following inter herd aggression. This was confirmed with the AV
when called. AV stated a video was provided to her showing an adult cavy rushing after it to which it attempted to bite.
The AV stated this animal was the infant cavy that had to be euthanized due to its injuries. AV stated aggression among
the herd were noted following changes made by the facility in regards to feeding.
During inspection an adult female Patagonian cavy named Ginger was observed with a healing laceration. The laceration
was superficial, measuring approximately 5 inches in length, and was surrounded by clipped fur. The skin had a few
raised and red pinpoint lesions that had scabbed over. The facility representatives stated the wounds were first seen on
6/27/26 but were unsure how she obtained them. Additionally, there were two brief incidents seen on inspection where
Ginger was observed chasing off another adult female Patagonian Cavy who was near her offspring.
Housing incompatible animals together in the same primary enclosure can lead to stress, injury, and even death. Animals
housed in the same primary enclosure must be compatible. Animals shall not be housed near animals that interfere with
their health or cause them discomfort.
Correct from this date forward, June 30, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
